newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Jewish settlers move caravans into West Bank.
newsitem.headline: Jewish settlers move caravans into West Bank.

text.p: Witnesses said Jewish settlers moved mobile homes onto a West Bank hilltop on Friday to try to expand a settlement in the Israeli-occupied territory, a move condemned by Palestinians and Israeli peace activists.

The action, which an adviser to Palestinian President Yasser Arafat called "provocative", occurred as Israeli-Palestinian talks on a long-delayed Israeli troop pullback in the West Bank town of Hebron remained stalled.
"This is a protest action," said Aharon Domb, spokesman for the Jewish settler umbrella group Yesha. "There is a bitter spirit between Yesha and the Prime Minister (Benjamin Netanyahu)."
Arafat adviser Ahmed Tibi told Reuters: "This is a serious and a provocative move. The Israeli government must put an end to this serious threat to the peace process."
Domb said Beit El settlers were upset that they had not received an answer from Netanyahu to their request to expand the settlement.
"They waited patiently for three or four weeks. When no answer came, they decided to go up the hill."

The settlers moved seven mobile homes to the hill about one km (half a mile) from Beit El, near the PLO-ruled town of Ramallah, under cover of darkness. Palestinians said the land belonged to Arabs from the villages of Ein Yabrud, Dura al-Qare and Jalazoun.
A Reuters photographer said some 200 settlers gathered around the mobile homes, where they had moved a refrigerator, generators and a children's jungle gym.
Israel's army radio said the site had been declared a closed military area and security forces would disperse the settlers, but an army spokesman could not immediately confirm the report.
Witnesses said the Israeli army put a ring of soldiers between the hilltop and the nearby Arab village of Ein Yabrud but did not try to stop the settlers.
Israel's leading Peace Now movement condemned the action and called on Netanyahu to remove the settlers.

"The Peace Now movement requests from the prime minister and defence minister to immediately order the removal of the settlers that are acting illegally," Peace Now spokesman Allon Arnon told Reuters.
Jewish settlers tried to take over the same hill in 1995 but were evacuated by force by Israel's previous government.
